newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN COACH FEARS GERMAN CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEVERKUSEN COACH FEARS GERMAN CHAMPIONS.

text.p: German league leaders Bayer Leverkusen hope to head into the winter break this weekend at the top but their coach Christoph Daum fears the country's most dangerous club when the Bundesliga resumes in February.
Reigning champions Borussia Dortmund have struggled with injuries this season and are presently fourth, two points behind Leverkusen and Bayern Munich, who are level on goal difference.
But Daum, who led VfB Stuttgart to the title in 1992, said the European Cup quarter-finalists have the potential to mount a major challenge when the league re-opens after Sunday's shutdown.
"Dortmund are in the quarter-finals of the European Cup again. As far as I'm concerned Ottmar Hitzfeld's team is also the top favourite for the championship," Daum said.
"They have the biggest potential to improve. If they can avoid injuries in the second half of the season they can really lift their form more than anyone else."

Going into the break at the top gives any side a major psychological boost. It is well known that the team which leads at halfway -- known in Germany as the "Autumn Champions" -- usually wins the crown.
Leverkusen and Dortmund have the most difficult games of the leading four teams this weekend.
Bayer travel on Friday to sixth-placed Bochum, who have surprised many with their good form this year after promotion. Dortmund also face a difficult trip to fifth-placed Cologne on Saturday.
Bayern host struggling Borussia Moenchengladbach while third-placed Stuttgart travel to lowly Armenia Bielefeld. Both games are on Saturday.
Bayern managed a 1-1 draw at Stuttgart, the most impressive team of the first half of the season, in their top-of-the-table clash last Sunday.
But the Bavarians' goal tally has been very disappointing this season with national team captain Juergen Klinsmann struggling to make an impact.
Chairman Franz Beckenbauer has warned that they must produce a great deal more in the second half.
The mood at the club was given a boost, however, on Thursday when coach Giovanni Trapattoni said he was not a candidate for the vacant job of Italy trainer.
"I have a contract with Bayern and respect this contract. That is not a problem for me," said the former Juventus, Internazionale and AC Milan trainer.
Bayern vice-chairman Karl-Heinz Rummenigge added he could imagine Bayern striking a new deal with the coach after his present contract ends in June 1998.

Bayern go into Saturday's clash without international defender-cum-libero Thomas Helmer who underwent an operation on a gallstone problem on Wednesday. Goalkeeper Oliver Kahn is also doubtful because of a groin strain.
Leverkusen should be at full strength for Friday's game.
